description: The map n to the integer class of (n,0) is injective and preserves addition, multiplication, zero, one, and order.
signature:
Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.natural_integer_embedding :
  (Function.Injective fun n => Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerClass n 0) ∧
    (∀ (m n : ℕ),
        Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerAdd (Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerClass m 0)
            (Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerClass n 0) =
          Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerClass (m + n) 0) ∧
      (∀ (m n : ℕ),
          Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerMul (Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerClass m 0)
              (Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerClass n 0) =
            Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerClass (m * n) 0) ∧
        (∀ (m n : ℕ),
            Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.IntegerLE (Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerClass m 0)
                (Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerClass n 0) ↔
              m ≤ n) ∧
          Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerValue (Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerClass 0 0) = 0 ∧
            Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerValue (Lemmatheca.SetTheory.NumberSystems.integerClass 1 0) = 1
